source_text: Hunccine audere dicere se damnatorem non esse coniugii, et tanto scelere illudere auribus imperitis, et a Manichaei se dicat recessisse consortio, qui commixtionem sexuum, qui operam nuptiarum, qui affectionem et sensum parentum in regno diaboli multiplici professione constituit; atque ad haec inventa Manichaei adiutorium sui acuminis iungens, pronuntiat quidem diabolicam commixtionem, eamque esse et opere et carne coniugum, ac propter eam deputat regno diaboli, absolutis tamen operatoribus, innocentes. Ita utique Deo semper infestus, diabolo, sicut dicit, per libidinem servientes tuetur.
pass_a_gloss: Does this man dare to say he is not a condemner of marriage, and with so great a crime mock unskilled ears, and say he has receded from the fellowship of Manichaeus, who established by a multiple profession the mingling of the sexes, the work of marriages, the affection and sense of parents in the kingdom of the devil; and joining to these inventions of Manichaeus the help of his own sharpness, he pronounces indeed a diabolical mingling, and that it is both by the work and by the flesh of spouses, and on account of it he assigns to the kingdom of the devil, the workers nevertheless having been acquitted, the innocents. Thus, always hostile to God, he protects those serving the devil, as he says, through lust.

LS nuptiae; Blaise Christian marriage as God's work
LS libido; Blaise pudenda libido vs nuptiae

pass_b_english: Does this man dare to say he does not condemn marriage, to mock uneducated ears with such wickedness, and to claim that he has withdrawn from Manichaeus’s company? By repeated professions he places the union of the sexes, the act of marriage, and the parents’ feeling and sensation within the devil’s kingdom. Adding the help of his own sharpness to these Manichaean inventions, he pronounces the union devilish, located in both the act and the flesh of the married couple. Yet because of it he assigns the innocent to the devil’s kingdom, while acquitting those who perform the act! Always hostile to God in this way, he defends those who, according to him, serve the devil through lust.

choices.why: Julian's pudenda libido is the appetite accompanying union, not a created substance of sin.
Julian defends marriage as God's work against the charge that generation transmits sin.
Julian's standing charge: natural evil is Manichaean. Keep the sect-name, not 'dualists'.
